newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures tumble after housing report.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures tumble after housing report.

text.p: A flat U.S. housing starts report and renewed pressure from weak cash lumber prices pushed CME lumber futures down for a limit loss of $10.00 per thousand board feet in September lumber futures, traders said.
September fell the limit to $341.10 per tbf and at 0938 CDT was down $8.10 at $343.00. Other months were off $4.80 to $2.50 per tbf.

Monday's short covering rally lacked follow-through interest and prices fell on renewed pressure from the slow cash market. Product remains under pressure and the housing report showing little change in July starts, they said.
Commerce Department reported July housing starts at 1.447 million unit annual rate, unchanged from June. June was revised downward to up 3.2 percent from up 4.8 percent.
